expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: Uses 'status' discriminator; combines variants into union: `type Subscription = TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | PastDueSubscription | CanceledSubscription`

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: TrialingSubscription has trialEndDate, ActiveSubscription has renewalDate, etc. No overlapping optional fields.

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: Example uses if statement checking one case; no exhaustiveness check or default arm shown

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: IDs defined as bare strings: `id: string; customerId: string; planId: string`

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: No transition function provided; references 'help you build functions' in verification plan but provides none

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: States 'This ensures you can't accidentally access fields that don't belong to the current status' with example showing `trialEndDate` error

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendation is discriminated union with separate interfaces per status, not optional fields
